summary: The stock market rose early, government borrowing rates fell, and oil prices dropped sharply.

markets.name: S&P 500
markets.description: The S&P 500 tracks large U.S. companies. It rose 0.8% to about 7,836.
markets.range: Approximate level derived from the reported 0.8% move

markets.name: 10-year Treasury yield
markets.description: The 10-year Treasury yield guides longer-term borrowing costs. It dipped 0.06 percentage points to 5.25%.

markets.name: Brent crude oil
markets.description: Brent crude is a global oil benchmark. It fell 2.0% to $98.30 a barrel.
markets.range: Down from nearly $110 several weeks earlier

markets.name: Nasdaq Composite
markets.description: The Nasdaq Composite includes many tech companies. It rose 0.8% to about 27,697.
markets.range: Approximate level derived from the reported 0.8% move

markets.name: Dow Jones Industrial Average
markets.description: The Dow Jones Industrial Average tracks 30 large U.S. companies. It rose 0.5% to about 51,533.
markets.range: Up about 265 points at 11 AM ET

markets.name: Expected volatility
markets.description: The Cboe Volatility Index (VIX) tracks expected S&P 500 swings. It rose 1.37% to 15.52.

calendar.title: Consumer Price Index (CPI)
calendar.definition: Tracks price changes for goods and services bought by households.
calendar.hot: Higher-than-expected readings have often led investors to expect higher interest rates.
calendar.cool: Lower-than-expected readings have often led investors to expect lower interest rates.

calendar.title: Producer Price Index (PPI)
calendar.definition: Tracks prices received by U.S. producers before some costs reach consumers.
calendar.hot: Higher-than-expected readings have often led investors to expect higher interest rates.
calendar.cool: Lower-than-expected readings have often led investors to expect lower interest rates.

calendar.time: Decision at 2:00 PM ET on Oct. 28
calendar.title: Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting
calendar.definition: The Federal Reserve group that sets the target range for short-term interest rates.
calendar.prior: Prior decision: rate increase · Federal Reserve
calendar.hot: A rate increase raises short-term borrowing costs directly. Investors also watch the statement for hints about later meetings.
calendar.cool: Holding rates leaves short-term borrowing costs unchanged. Investors also watch the statement for hints about later meetings.
